dialog_history.summary: Jane is struggling with the loss of communication and friendship with their close friend Lisa after lending her money and not being repaid, leading to feelings of isolation and difficulty focusing on work.

observation.content: The seeker lent some money to their friend Lisa months ago and hasn't been repaid yet.
Lisa has cut off all communication with the seeker.
The seeker used to frequently hang out with Lisa and now feels like they have lost a part of their life.
The seeker is having difficulty focusing on work and feels isolated.
The seeker used to enjoy painting but hasn't done it in a while.

dialogue.content: Hey Jane, how have you been holding up lately?
Hi. Not too great, to be honest. It's been a rough couple of weeks.
I'm really sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about what's been going on?
Well, do you remember Lisa? My friend I mentioned before?
Yes, I remember you talking about them. What's up with Lisa?
So, we've hit this weird and stressful snag. I lent her some money months ago and she hasn’t paid me back yet.
That definitely sounds stressful. How is it affecting your relationship with Lisa?
She's completely cut off communication with me. No calls, texts, nothing.
That must be really hard on you, especially since she was such a close friend.
It feels like losing a part of my life. We used to hang out all the time and now it's just silence.
It sounds like you're mourning the loss of that friendship. Have you had a chance to reach out or communicate with her recently?
I’ve tried. Sent a couple of messages, but they’ve gone unanswered.
It must feel really disappointing not to hear back. What do you miss most about your friendship with Lisa?
We used to bounce ideas off each other, and she was the first person I'd call when something great happened at work.
It's understandable to miss those shared moments and support. How are you managing everything else alongside this?
It's made focusing on work tough. I feel a bit isolated, honestly.
I'm so sorry you're feeling this way. Feeling isolated can really weigh on you. Is there anyone else you feel comfortable confiding in?
I haven't really opened up to anyone else about this. It's been hard admitting to myself how deep this issue has affected me.
It takes a lot of courage to open up. It's important to take time for yourself and process everything. Is there anything you can do to help ease your mind a bit right now?
Maybe get back into some hobbies. I used to enjoy painting but haven't done it in a while.
That sounds like a wonderful idea. Engaging in something creative can be really therapeutic. Would you like support picking it back up?
I think that would help. Just getting started again might lift this weight a little.
I'm here to support you with this. Whenever you're ready, you can share your progress, and I’d love to hear how it goes.
Thank you. It feels a bit better knowing someone’s there to listen. I appreciate it.
Anytime, Jane. You’re not alone in this. We'll take it one step at a time.

dialog_history.summary: The seeker is feeling anxious due to an unexpected car insurance bill and ongoing financial stress exacerbated by the loss of a friendship.

observation.content: The seeker unexpectedly owes more on her car insurance bill due to an oversight.
The seeker is feeling pretty anxious about the unexpected bill.
The seeker finds losing a friendship hard and adds to the stress of dealing with the bill.
The seeker is worried about falling behind on other payments and desires financial stability.
The seeker has not considered reaching out for financial advice due to a tendency to handle things alone.

dialogue.content: Hey, do you have a moment? I could use some support right now.
Of course, Jane. What's going on?
I just got hit with an unexpected bill, and it's really stressing me out.
I'm sorry to hear that. Financial stress can be so overwhelming. Do you want to talk more about the bill?
Yeah, it's for my car insurance. I thought I had paid it, but apparently, there was some sort of oversight, and now I owe more than I expected.
That sounds frustrating, especially when you're already stretched thin. How are you handling it so far?
Honestly, not well. I'm feeling pretty anxious about it because money has been tight lately, especially since the whole situation with my friend.
I remember you mentioned that. It must be tough still dealing with those effects. How does that add to your current stress?
It just feels like a never-ending cycle. Losing that friendship was hard, and now this bill feels like another setback.
That's completely understandable. It's like everything piles up at once. How are you coping with these feelings?
I've been trying to budget more strictly and cut unnecessary expenses, but unexpected things keep popping up.
That can make it feel like you're running in place, right? Are there any specific concerns you're dwelling on?
I'm worried I'll fall behind on other payments. I hate feeling this insecure financially. I just want to feel stable again.
It's such a difficult spot to be in. Maybe talking to someone about financial strategies or planning could help?
That's a good idea. I haven't really considered reaching out for advice yet. I'm always thinking I have to handle it alone.
It's okay to ask for help, Jane. You've been doing so much on your own. Sometimes, a fresh perspective makes all the difference.
I appreciate you saying that. I'll look into finding someone who can help with budgeting strategies.
I'm glad to hear that. You're handling this situation with a lot of grace, even if it doesn't feel like it right now.
Thanks. It helps to talk about it. I'm feeling a little more at ease just expressing what's been on my mind.
Anytime, Jane. I'm here for you whenever you need to talk.
I really appreciate it. I'll keep you updated on how things go with the financial advice.
Please do. Remember, you're not alone in this. You have people who care about you.

dialog_history.summary: The seeker is overwhelmed, anxious about financial issues and a broken friendship, and plans to use journaling to process her thoughts and emotions.

dialogue.content: Hey Jane, how are things going for you today?
Hi, I'm okay, I guess. I got a new journal today to help me figure things out.
That sounds like a positive step. What inspired you to start journaling?
Well, things have been pretty overwhelming lately with everything going on. I thought it might help me process my thoughts and emotions better.
It's great that you're taking proactive steps to manage your stress. Would you like to share more about what's been on your mind?
Sure. I've been really stressed about this money issue with my friend, or former friend now, and the unexpected bills that keep coming up.
That sounds really tough. Financial stress combined with losing a friend can be a lot to handle. How are you managing everything?
It's hard. I feel anxious most of the time. I'm constantly worried about my finances and how to make ends meet, especially with that insurance bill.
I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds like you're carrying a lot on your shoulders. Have you been able to find any moments of peace or relaxation lately?
Not really. I keep trying to focus on work to distract myself, but it's not really working out.
It must be difficult to juggle work with all these thoughts in your mind. Do you feel like journaling might help untangle some of them?
Yeah, I hope so. I haven't written in it yet, but I plan to start tonight. Maybe it will help clarify my feelings and guide me to some solutions.
Starting is often the hardest part, but it sounds like you're on the right track. Taking time for yourself can be really healing. What do you hope to gain from journaling?
I just hope to understand my emotions better and maybe find new perspectives on my situation. I'm also hoping to find some sense of control over things again.
That's a wonderful goal. Gaining insight into your emotions can provide clarity. Remember that you're not alone in this. I'm here to listen whenever you need to talk.
Thank you. It really helps to know that someone is here to listen.
Anytime, Jane. I'm glad you reached out today. Keep me updated on how the journaling goes, okay?
I will. Thanks for the support. It means a lot.
You're welcome. You're doing the best you can, and I'm proud of you for taking steps towards self-care. Take care and talk soon!

dialog_history.summary: Seeker is anxious about job performance and fears being viewed as incompetent due to not meeting work speed expectations.

dialogue.content: I am worried about being perfect on my job.  I don't want to lose my job.
I hear you are trying to be perfect on your job because you are worried about losing your job.  How long have you been at your job?
I have been working for about 4 months, but I just am not as fast at it as everyone else.  I'm trying so hard working late and everything but it's never enough.
That can be hard when you are working so hard to try to do your best.  Can you consult with a supervisor or co-workers to get some help?
Maybe I could ask my friend and co-worker for some tips.  I'm a little embarrassed to do so, but don't know where to turn. I don't want to get fired.
Asking for help isn't always a bad thing.  I asked for help at my last job and they gave me someone to help out.  I was so relieved.
That's true maybe it could turn out for the better.  But what if they see me as incompetant?
I can see that you have worry of being seen incompetent but as long as you are doing your best, they have to see the efforts you are making as positive.
That's a good way to put it.
Sometimes deep breaths can help keep you calm when approaching others in an anxiety provoking situation.
I will have to try that.  That might help.
Have you thought of doing additional work related trainings?  Sometimes they can give suggestions to improve work abilities.
That sounds great.  Do you think my work would be supportive?
Work can often pay for trainings or offer suggestions what may improve work strategies.
Wow, I hope I can take advantage of that.  I will have to check into that.  Who should I approach at work?
You could ask your immediate supervisor or sometimes Human resources for support.
I can do that.  I think I'll reach out tomorrow to Human Resources for some help.
That sounds like a good plan to reach out for support.  Is there anything else I can help with?
No that should be all.  I am feeling more confident in strategies to use to help me.  Thanks
You are very welcome.

The seeker lost a friend named Lisa due to issues related to money.

dialogue.content: Hi, just needed someone to talk to.
Hi Jane! Of course, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I had my performance review at work today... and it wasn't great.
I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds like it must be really tough to hear. How are you feeling about it?
I'm feeling anxious and a bit of self-doubt creeping in. I thought I was handling everything okay.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. It seems like there's been a lot on your plate recently. Would you like to talk more about it?
I guess everything's just been snowballing since the thing with Lisa. I still can't believe how it all fell apart.
Losing a friend, especially over something like money, can feel really isolating. How has it been affecting you lately?
It's made focusing on work harder. And getting hit with that unexpected bill last month didn't help. Everything feels out of control.
It sounds like you're dealing with a lot of financial and emotional stress right now. It's a lot for anyone to handle. How have you been coping with it all?
I started writing in a journal. It helps sometimes, but the stress keeps piling up. I thought it would get better by now.
Journaling can be a great outlet. It's important to give yourself grace with everything happening. You're doing your best in a really challenging time.
Thank you. I keep telling myself that, but it's hard to believe it sometimes. I just wish things would turn around.
It makes sense to want things to improve quickly. Progress can be slow, but you're taking steps in the right direction by reaching out and processing everything going on.
Yeah, it helps to talk about it. I suppose I need to take it one day at a time.
Absolutely. It's like building a path through all these challenges— day by day, step by step. You have the strength to navigate this, even if it doesn't feel like it sometimes.
I really appreciate your support. It makes things feel a bit less overwhelming.
I'm glad to be here for you. Remember, you're not alone in this. We can keep talking anytime you need.
Thanks a lot. I might take you up on that.
Anytime, Jane. Take care of yourself, and reach out whenever you need to.
Will do. Take care, too.

dialog_history.summary: The seeker, Jane, is experiencing stress and anxiety due to financial issues, a challenging work situation, and a personal fallout with a friend named Lisa.

The seeker received a poor performance review last week which affected her confidence.
The seeker uses a journal to manage stress but still feels anxious.
The seeker feels angry and sad about how things ended with her friend Lisa.

dialogue.content: Hi Jane, how have you been feeling lately?
Hey, it's been tough, honestly. I've been dealing with a lot of stress and barely sleeping.
I'm so sorry to hear that. Stress and insomnia can really take a toll. What's been weighing on you the most?
It's a mix of things... Financial issues, work, and I guess, the whole fallout with Lisa.
Losing a friend over money is really difficult. Do you want to talk more about what's been going on with work as well?
Yeah, I had a poor performance review last week, and it shook my confidence. It's hard to focus when my mind is elsewhere.
That sounds really challenging, especially when you're already feeling anxious. Have you noticed any patterns or triggers for the stress?
I think it's the feeling of everything piling up at once. Every little thing just feels like too much now.
When it all becomes overwhelming, it's so important to prioritize taking care of yourself. Have you been able to use your journal to help manage the stress?
Yes, I try to write in it every night. It does help to put my thoughts on paper, but sometimes the anxiety is just too strong.
It's good that you're using your journal as a tool. It's natural to still feel overwhelmed, especially given everything you're handling right now.
Thanks. I know you’re right, but sometimes I just feel so alone in this.
You’re definitely not alone, Jane. I'm here for you, and it’s okay to reach out whenever you need someone to listen.
I really appreciate that. It’s comforting to have someone to talk to.
Do you have any plans to tackle the financial stress, or is there someone who could help you navigate that?
I’ve been looking into budgeting more strictly, but it’s tough. I think I just feel angry and sad about how things ended with Lisa.
It's understandable to feel that guilt, but you're doing your best under challenging circumstances. It's important to be gentle with yourself.
Yeah, I know logically I did what I could, but emotionally it’s hard to let go.
Emotions can be tough to navigate, but it’s a process. Small steps are still progress. Have you been able to find moments of peace or relaxation?
I try to meditate a bit or take a walk when I can. It helps, even if just a little.
That's great! Even small moments of peace can accumulate and make a difference over time. You're doing really well to manage through this.
Thank you. It means a lot to hear that, especially when I feel like I'm drowning.
Always happy to remind you. You’re stronger than you realize, and it takes courage to face these challenges.
I hope things will start to turn around soon. I'm trying to keep faith.
Holding onto hope is incredibly powerful. And remember, you’re not alone - I’m here cheering you on every step of the way.

dialogue.content: Hi Jane, it's great to hear from you again. How have you been holding up?
Hi, it's been a bit rough lately. My car broke down and the repair costs are just... more than I can handle right now.
Oh no, I'm so sorry to hear that, Jane. That must be incredibly stressful, especially with everything else you've had to deal with recently.
It really is. I've been trying to manage, but the financial stress keeps piling up. I still haven't resolved the money issue with my friend, and now this... It's overwhelming.
I can only imagine how difficult that must be. You've been doing your best under such challenging circumstances. It's okay to feel overwhelmed.
Thank you. Sometimes it feels like I'm just not able to catch a break. I've been trying to keep track of everything with my journal, but it feels like every day brings something new.
Journaling is a great tool, and it's a good step that you're using it to process your thoughts and feelings. It shows how you're trying to find ways to cope.
Yeah, I thought it might help calm my anxieties. But with my job performance not being where it's supposed to be, and money problems, I just feel stuck.
Feeling stuck is definitely tough. It's important to remember that it's not a reflection of your abilities or worth. You're dealing with a lot, and your efforts are meaningful.
Thanks. Sometimes I just worry that I'm not living up to expectations, especially at work. The fear of being seen as incompetent is always there.
I understand. Work pressure can be intense, and when combined with personal challenges, it's a lot to balance. Have you been able to talk to anyone at work about how you're feeling?
Not yet. I'm hesitant because I don't want it to seem like I'm making excuses. I really want to prove myself and get back on track.
That makes sense. It might help to reach out for support when you're ready, even just to get some feedback. Sometimes, opening up can bring understanding and solutions you couldn't see before.
You're right. I'll think about that. Maybe just having a conversation could help put things into perspective.
Absolutely, even small steps can lead to positive changes. Remember, you're doing the best you can, and it's okay to seek help when you need it.
I will try to remember that. It's helpful to talk about it and just get it off my chest a bit.
I'm glad you reached out, Jane. It's important to have a space where you feel heard. If you ever need to talk or get things off your mind, I'm here.
Thank you so much. It really means a lot to have someone who listens and understands.
You're welcome. Remember, one step at a time, and be gentle with yourself. You're not alone in this, and there are brighter days ahead.
I'll keep that in mind. Thanks again for your support.

dialog_history.summary: Seeker feels overwhelmed by work pressure and financial issues, considering switching to a less stressful job after a November performance review led to self-doubt.

dialogue.content: Hey there, can we chat for a bit?

I remember you mentioned being anxious about your job performance a few months ago. It sounds like everything's been piling up.
Exactly. I try to keep up, but it feels like I’m always falling short. The stress is just too much sometimes.

I've also been dealing with financial pressures ever since my car broke down. There always seems to be another expense around the corner.
I can imagine how stressful that must be for you. Those financial strains can really add a lot of pressure.
Yeah, and the thing with my friend cutting me off because of the money didn’t help either. It all feels connected somehow.
It must have been tough losing a friend on top of everything else. You’re really going through so much at once.
I just keep thinking about switching to something less stressful, maybe something that allows me more flexibility.
That makes a lot of sense. Flexibility can certainly alleviate some stress, offering you both space and time for yourself.
I've been trying to track my thoughts in that new journal I got. It's been helpful sometimes, but the change feels daunting.
Journaling is a great way to process thoughts and emotions. Taking things one step at a time with any big decision can help it feel less overwhelming.
I’ll try to keep that in mind. Just voicing it all out helps me see things a bit clearer.
I’m glad to hear that, Jane. You’re not alone in this, and I’m here to support you in any way I can.
Thank you so much. Having someone listen without judgment really makes a difference.
Anytime, Jane. You’re handling this with strength, and I’m here whenever you need to talk.

dialog_history.summary: The seeker feels overwhelmed by her sister Eliza's engagement, compounded by work stress, financial issues, past breakup anxiety, and feelings of loneliness, leading her to consider seeking professional help.

dialogue.content: Hey, I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed today.
Hi Jane, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
My sister Eliza just announced her engagement.
Oh wow, that must be a big piece of news for the family. How are you processing it?
I'm happy for her, truly, but it also makes me reflect on where I am in my life.
It's completely natural to have mixed feelings. Have you been able to talk to Eliza about how you're feeling?
Not yet. I don’t want to dampen her excitement with my own worries.
That's considerate of you. How has this news been affecting you emotionally?
I feel lonely, to be honest. Recently, things haven't been great for me...work stress, financial issues...it's cumulative.
That sounds really challenging. You've been through a lot lately. Remember, it's okay to feel this way.
There’s also the lingering anxiety from my last breakup, and then seeing Eliza so happy makes me question my own happiness.
Breakups can be incredibly tough, and comparing situations is a natural response. But your journey is unique and just as important.
Thanks for saying that. I guess I need to focus on myself more, but it's hard with all the stress.
It seems like a lot is demanding your attention. Maybe you could lean into that journaling habit you started?
That's a good idea. I haven’t been consistent, but I think it helps when I do it.
Starting small is perfectly fine. You're doing your best and that's what matters. Have you considered talking to a professional about everything you've been facing?
I've thought about it. It might be time to reach out for more help. Just to sort through everything.
I think that could be really beneficial. You're taking important steps by recognizing where you are. You're not alone in this.
Thanks, I appreciate that. Just expressing these feelings openly has been a relief.
I'm glad to hear that. I'm always here to listen. Take care of yourself, Jane.

dialog_history.summary: Jane is struggling with the aftermath of a significant argument with her sister Eliza about her involvement in planning Eliza's wedding, causing feelings of misunderstanding and sadness.

observation.content: Jane had a huge argument with her sister, Eliza, while planning Eliza's wedding.
Jane feels that her sister does not appreciate her suggestions.
Jane's sister accused her of trying to control everything.
Jane feels terrible and worries she is not being supportive of her sister.
Jane feels awkward about attending her sister's wedding due to the conflict.
Jane recalls past conflicts with her sister where they eventually managed to mend things.
Jane believes that writing in her journal could help her process her emotions.

dialogue.content: Hi Jane, how are you holding up lately?
Hey, not the best to be honest. Things aren't getting any better.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
It's mostly about my sister, Eliza. We had a huge argument while planning her wedding.
I'm really sorry to hear that. It can be tough when someone close to you is involved. What happened?
She just doesn't appreciate my suggestions. I was only trying to help, but she took it the wrong way.
That sounds frustrating, especially when you're just trying to be helpful. How did she react?
She accused me of trying to control everything and said I wasn't being supportive.
It must be really hurtful to feel misunderstood like that. How are you feeling about it now?
I feel terrible. I love her and want to be there for her, but now it seems I've done the opposite.
Remember, it's not always easy to navigate these situations. Has this tension changed how you feel about attending the wedding?
A bit, yeah. I was looking forward to being part of it, but now it feels awkward.
It's understandable to feel conflicted. Being part of her big day is important, but so is your peace of mind.
Exactly. I just worry that our relationship might not be the same after this.
Are there moments from the past where you've overcome conflicts together?
Yes, there were times we've disagreed but always managed to mend things eventually.
That's promising. Perhaps this can be mended over time too. Do you think talking to her calmly might help?
Maybe. I guess I need to find the right time and words to explain my intentions.
That sounds like a thoughtful approach. Taking time to sort out your feelings first could also be beneficial.
Yes, I think writing about it in my journal could help me process everything.
That's a great idea, Jane. The journal seems like a good outlet for you.
Thanks. It always helps me get things off my chest and see things more clearly.
You have a lot on your plate right now, but I'm confident you'll find a way to navigate through it.
I hope so. Thanks for listening. It makes a difference knowing someone understands.
I'm always here for you, Jane. Whenever you need someone to talk to, just reach out.
I really appreciate that. Talk to you soon.
Take care. Remember to be gentle with yourself.
I will. Thank you!

dialog_history.summary: Jane is reflecting on a recent emotional conversation with her friend Eliza about wedding-related stress and feels closer to Eliza after reconciling their issues.

observation.content: Jane and Eliza had an emotional conversation a few days ago that involved tears and relief.
Jane feels closer to Eliza after admitting mutual stress over wedding planning.
Jane and Eliza have agreed to communicate openly, making wedding planning feel more like a partnership.
Jane has started journaling again to sort through her feelings.
Jane is attempting to address her financial stress proactively.

dialogue.content: Hey, feeling a bit all over the place today. Mind if I share?
Of course, Jane. I'm here to listen. What's been going on?

Yes, you’ve mentioned feeling misunderstood during that time. How are things between you two now?
We actually had a really deep conversation a few days ago. Lots of tears but good ones, I think.
That sounds intense but potentially healing. How did that feel for you?
It was a mix of relief and lingering sadness. I’m happy we cleared the air, but all those pent-up emotions were exhausting.
It makes sense to feel drained after such a heart-to-heart. It's brave of you both to confront those emotions together.
Thanks. I just wish it didn't have to get so messy before getting better.
Relationships can be messy, but the reconciling part is important. How’s your perspective on everything now?
I feel closer to her actually. We both admitted how much the wedding planning has stressed us out.
That’s insightful. Acknowledging shared stress can bring people together. How’s the wedding planning going now?
Better. We’ve agreed to communicate openly about decisions. It feels more like a partnership now, rather than me just helping her.
That’s great to hear, Jane. Open communication is key in any relationship.
Yeah, I've also started journaling again. It helps sort through these complicated feelings.
Journaling is a great tool. How does writing about your thoughts and emotions help you?
It gives me clarity. Putting pen to paper makes everything feel less overwhelming and more manageable.
I’m glad it’s helping you. Have you noticed any other changes since you reconciled with Eliza?
I feel a bit lighter emotionally. Mending the rift with her feels like a burden lifted.
That’s a beautiful way to put it. Rebuilding that connection must feel rewarding.
It does. I’m also trying to be more proactive about addressing my financial stress instead of letting it control me.
That’s a positive step forward. You've been through a lot, and it’s important to take care of yourself too.
Trying my best. It’s a work in progress, you know? Balancing everything is tough.
Absolutely. You’re making great progress, even if it doesn’t always feel that way. I’m here whenever you need to talk.
Thank you, that means a lot. I’ll keep leaning on you if that's okay.
Always, Jane. Your journey is important, and I’m here to support you along the way.

dialog_history.summary: The seeker is struggling with resurfacing emotions from a past relationship's infidelity and feeling overwhelmed by stress from life events, causing anxiety and sleep disturbances.

observation.content: The seeker recently attended a social event that reminded her of past relationships.
The seeker is questioning if she's truly moved on from her past relationship.
The seeker is considering switching jobs but fears instability.
The seeker feels a bit left behind due to her sister's engagement.
The seeker has reconciled with her sister Eliza and they are in a good place now.
The seeker experiences insomnia as she feels unsettled with her current situation.
The seeker has been journaling to cope with stress but finds it overwhelming.

dialogue.content: Hey there, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Jane. What's on your mind?
I attended a social event recently, and it unearthed some emotions I thought I had tucked away.
It sounds like it was quite an experience. What happened that brought these feelings to the surface?
I met someone there who reminded me of my past relationships, particularly the one that ended in a mess due to infidelity.
That must have been tough to be reminded of. How did it feel encountering someone who brought those memories back?
It was like reliving a bit of that heartache. I was both fascinated and apprehensive.
That's understandable. Did this interaction lead you to reflect on your past relationship?
Yes. I wondered if I've truly moved on or just buried the feelings. And with everything else, the stress seems unending.
Between work, financial pressures, and this emotional trigger, it sounds like you're carrying a heavy load.
Exactly. I've been thinking about switching jobs, but the fear of instability holds me back.
It's a significant decision. Finding a balance between what you want and need is crucial.
And my sister's engagement has been on my mind too. I'm genuinely happy for her, but I can't help feeling a little left behind.
It's okay to feel those mixed emotions. How are you and Eliza doing since you mended things?
We're in a good place now. She really understood where I was coming from after we talked things out.
That's wonderful to hear. Having her support must mean a lot.
It definitely does. I just wish I felt more settled with everything else. All these thoughts keep me up at night.
Insomnia can really take a toll. How have you been coping with the stress?
I've been journaling to process my thoughts, but it's been a rollercoaster.
Writing can be therapeutic, but it sounds like there's more weighing on you.
Yeah, all of it combined just overwhelms me sometimes.
Jane, remember it's okay to seek help. Talking to someone professionally might help make things more manageable.
You might be right. It feels reassuring to know there are options out there.
Absolutely. You're not alone in this, and taking steps to care for yourself is important.
Thanks. I appreciate knowing there's someone who understands.
Anytime, Jane. You're doing the best you can, and that's enough.

dialog_history.summary: The seeker, Jane, experienced anxiety and anger when her ex, Jack, attempted to contact her, which resurfaced feelings from their past toxic relationship and is overwhelmed by work and financial stress.

observation.content: The seeker felt anxiety and anger when Jack contacted her.
The seeker is afraid of falling back into unhealthy habits from her past relationship with Jack.
The seeker is stressed by work and financial pressures and finds everything overwhelming.
The seeker sometimes uses journaling to manage her feelings but currently struggles with focus and sleep.
The seeker tries breathing exercises but struggles with a racing mind at night.
The seeker is concerned about the cost of therapy due to her financial situation.

dialogue.content: Hi, I really need to talk.
Of course, Jane. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
It's about Jack. He tried reaching out to me again, and it really threw me off.
I'm sorry to hear that, Jane. How did you feel when he contacted you?
Honestly, I felt a wave of anxiety and a bit of anger. I thought I was moving on, you know?
That sounds really tough. It's understandable to have those feelings, especially when someone from your past re-emerges unexpectedly.
Yeah, it's like all those feelings I had during our breakup came rushing back.
Breakups can leave a lasting impact, especially if things ended with unresolved issues. What worries you the most about Jack reaching out?
I guess I'm afraid of falling back into habits that were bad for me, like constantly questioning myself. We had a pretty toxic dynamic at times.
It's important that you're aware of the impact he had on you. It sounds like you're protecting yourself, which is a good step.
I'm trying. But it's hard when I think of all the other stressors in my life, like work and money. Everything feels so overwhelming.
It must be really challenging juggling all these pressures at once. Have you found anything that helps you manage when things get overwhelming?
Writing in my journal sometimes helps, but lately, I find it hard to focus or even sleep well.
Journaling is a great tool, and it's understandable that sleep and focus might be affected by anxiety. Do you have any relaxation techniques that help at night?
I try breathing exercises, but my mind races a lot. Maybe I need to establish a better nighttime routine.
That sounds like a good idea. A consistent routine can sometimes make a difference. Have you considered reaching out for professional help to guide you through this?
I have thought about therapy, but I'm worried about the cost, especially with my financial situation.
That's a valid concern. Some therapists offer sliding scales or there may be community resources available. It might be worth exploring if it can help you find balance.
I'll look into it. Just talking to you has helped a bit already.
I'm really glad to hear that. I'm always here whenever you need to talk. Take it one step at a time, Jane.
Thank you. It feels good to know I'm not alone in this.

dialog_history.summary: The seeker is feeling overwhelmed with a promotion offer that requires relocating overseas and grappling with fears of failure, leaving her family, and the impact on her relationship with Eliza.

observation.content: The seeker received a promotion offer.
The promotion offer requires relocating overseas.
The seeker has mixed feelings about moving overseas, fearing failure and leaving everything behind.
The seeker recently started getting along again with a family member named Eliza.
The seeker has not yet discussed the relocation with Eliza, fearing she may feel abandoned.

dialogue.content: Hey, are you available to chat?
Hi Jane! I'm here. What's going on?
I don't know, it's just been a lot lately. I got a promotion offer, but there's a catch.
Congratulations on the promotion offer! But what’s the catch?
Thanks. It means relocating overseas. I’m feeling pretty overwhelmed.
That's a big decision. It sounds like there's a lot to consider. How are you feeling about moving overseas?
Honestly, I have mixed feelings. It's a great opportunity, but I’m scared of leaving everything behind. What if I fail?

It’s completely natural to feel that way. You've been through a lot of stressful situations before, remember when you had the falling out with your friend over the money issue, and you managed to handle it?
True, I did handle that. But this feels different, like if I accept, everything changes.
Change can be daunting, but it also can be exciting. Deep down, what does your gut tell you?
A part of me wants to embrace this challenge. But I worry about my family, especially Eliza after we just started getting along again.
It's understandable to worry about your relationship with Eliza. Have you talked to her about this yet?
Not yet. I'm afraid she’ll feel like I'm abandoning her right when things are starting to get better between us.
Maybe having an open conversation with Eliza would help. She might surprise you with her support, especially after you both mended fences.
You’re right. I should probably talk to her. I just don't want to ruin anything.
It sounds like your relationship is stronger than you think. Keeping communication open could help strengthen it further.
I hope so. Moving would also mean leaving behind memories, and part of me is afraid of the unknown.
The unknown can be intimidating, but it also holds a lot of potential. It sounds like you’re searching for a balance between embracing new opportunities and holding onto what you value.
That's exactly it. I want to grow and advance my career, but I don't want to lose myself in the process.
You’re approaching this thoughtfully. Trust yourself to find that balance. Sometimes writing down your thoughts, like in your journal, might help clarify things.
That’s a good idea. Journaling helped last time. Maybe it will help me weigh the pros and cons more clearly this time too.
Absolutely. You’ve navigated tough situations before, and you've come out stronger each time. No matter what you decide, you’re capable of handling it.
Thank you. That means a lot. I guess I just needed to talk it out.
Anytime, Jane. Just remember, you’re not alone in this. I’m here for you, and so is your support network.
Thanks, I’ll reach out if I need more advice. Take care.
You too, Jane. Keep me posted on what you decide.

dialog_history.summary: The seeker is experiencing mixed feelings and anxiety after receiving a message from an old friend they had a falling out with last year due to a money situation.

observation.content: The seeker has not spoken to their old friend since a money situation last year.
The seeker finds it tough to shake off how the friendship ended.
The seeker associates the past friendship with times of job performance stress and financial stress.

dialogue.content: Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Jane. What's on your mind?
I got a message out of the blue from someone I used to be really close with. It's brought up so many mixed feelings.
That sounds complicated. Who was it, if you don't mind sharing?
It was from my old friend, who I haven't spoken to since the whole money situation last year.
Ah, I remember you mentioned them before. It's understandable that you'd feel a bit caught off guard.
Yeah, exactly. Part of me is nostalgic, but another part of me is wary. I don't want to go through that emotional turmoil again.
It's natural to have those feelings when someone from the past reaches out, especially given what transpired.
I just can't shake off the memory of how it ended. Losing a friend like that was tough.
It must've been really hard. Do you feel like you're ready to respond, or do you need more time to process?
I'm really unsure. A part of me misses the friendship, but I'm scared of being hurt again.
Both of those feelings make a lot of sense. It's important to protect your heart while also honoring what used to be.
Right. I also think back to how stressful things were—like with my job performance review and financial stress. It was too much.
Those were tough times for you. It shows how much strength it took for you to get through them.
Thanks. I guess I'm just worried that engaging in any more complicated relationships could bring back old stressors.
I completely understand your apprehension. Do you think setting boundaries might help if you decide to reconnect?
That might be a good idea. It could prevent past issues from repeating.
And if you ever feel overwhelmed, remember you can always pause and take the time you need.
You're right. I'll think about what I want and maybe draft a response if that time comes.
That sounds like a solid plan. It's all about doing what's best for you.
Thanks for listening. I just needed to get that off my chest.
Anytime, Jane. I'm here if you need to talk more.

dialog_history.summary: The seeker is grappling with mixed emotions about losing an overseas promotion, feeling both relieved and disappointed, and unsure about her future career growth at her current job.

observation.content: The seeker was stressing about an overseas promotion opportunity.

The seeker finds journaling helpful for tracking feelings and worries.

dialogue.content: Hey, could really use someone to talk to right now.

Well, they filled it with someone else without even informing me.
Wow, I'm really sorry to hear that. That must be so frustrating. How are you feeling about it?
I don't know... It's like a mix of relief and disappointment? I was anxious about moving, but also excited for the chance, you know?
It's completely understandable to feel that way. It's a significant life change that was suddenly altered. Have you had a chance to talk to your manager about it yet?
Not yet, I just found out through a colleague. Not exactly the news I was expecting today.
That sounds tough, especially finding out like that. It's important to voice how this has affected you. Are you planning to address it soon?
I will. I guess I'm nervous about how it might impact my growth here. I feel kind of stuck.

It's okay to feel uncertain about the future. But remember, you're resilient and have navigated through challenges before. Just like when you processed things with Eliza or dealt with the unexpected bill.
Yeah, that's true. I guess I've been through a lot already. I just keep wondering if it's worth staying at this job.

Thinking about your options is a smart move. Maybe reflecting on what you truly want in your career could help clarify things. Sometimes, journaling can help sort out these thoughts—still finding it useful?
Yes, the journal's been great. It helps me track my feelings and worries. It's like my own little therapist.
I'm glad to hear that. Remember, your happiness and fulfillment at work are crucial. And you're capable of figuring out the best path forward.
Thank you. It feels good just talking this out. It's like unloading a bit of the burden.
I'm always here to listen. You're never alone in this. Have you thought about what might come next, or do you need some time to digest everything?
I think I need a bit more time to let it all sink in. Maybe see how things unfold with work and talk it through with Eliza, too.
Taking your time sounds wise. And involving Eliza is a great idea, especially since you've grown closer recently. You always have people in your corner.
Yeah, I'll try open up to her more. Thank you again—it's helped more than you know.
Anytime, Jane. You're making progress, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.
That means a lot. I'll keep you posted on what happens. Thanks again!

dialog_history.summary: Jane feels betrayed and undervalued at work after finding out through unofficial channels that she missed out on an overseas promotion she was previously offered.

observation.content: Jane discovered she missed out on an overseas promotion she was previously offered.

Jane was concerned about how the overseas move would affect her relationship with Eliza.

Jane lacks confidence in having her concerns taken seriously by her manager after last year’s performance review.
Jane is considering discussing her situation with a trusted colleague for advice.

dialogue.content: Hey, can I vent about something?
Of course, Jane. What's on your mind?
I just found out I missed out on the overseas promotion I was offered a while back.
Oh no, that's really disappointing, especially after having been offered it. How are you feeling about it?
Honestly, I feel a bit betrayed. No one even told me; I just found out through the grapevine.
That sounds really tough, Jane. It's hard to be left out of the loop like that. How are you coping with all these emotions?
I'm trying to process it, but it's hard not to feel like it's a reflection of my value at work.
It's understandable to feel that way. Your work and contributions are valuable, even if it doesn't feel like it right now. Do you want to talk more about what led to this?
I think it's a combination of things. There was so much going on—my anxiety, all the financial stress, and then this on top of it.
It's a lot to deal with, for sure. It reminds me of when you were considering the promotion and feeling overwhelmed. Do you think those feelings had an impact?
Maybe. I was really torn about the decision, fearing how it would affect my relationship with Eliza and just leaving everything behind.
It's such a big decision with lots of factors to weigh. It makes sense that it took a toll on you. How are you feeling about your relationship with Eliza now, after everything?
We’ve been better. We managed to patch things up after the wedding planning fallout, but I wonder how she’d have reacted if I moved.
It sounds like your bond with her is important to you. Maybe those fears were valid, but it's good to hear you've reconciled. How do you see your career moving forward after this setback?
It's hard to say. I feel stuck, but in some ways, relieved I don't have to move overseas. Yet, there's this nagging fear I'll remain stagnant in my career.
It’s definitely a complex situation. Being relieved but also worried about stagnation can be conflicting. Have you thought about discussing your career goals and concerns with your manager?
I have, but I'm hesitant. After the performance review last year, I just don't feel confident my concerns will be taken seriously.
It's tough to bring up concerns at work, especially after what happened. Is there someone you trust at work who might offer advice or support on how to approach your manager?
Maybe. There's a colleague I'm on good terms with. I might talk to them first and see how they handled similar situations.
That sounds like a good plan—having someone to bounce ideas off can make a big difference. Whatever you decide, I’m here to support you as you navigate this.
Thanks, I really appreciate it. It's just been a lot to process, but talking about it helps.
I'm glad talking it through helped a bit. Remember, you're not alone in this. Anytime you need to talk, I'm here.
Thanks, that means a lot. I’ll keep you posted on how things go. Talk soon?
Definitely. Take care of yourself, Jane.

dialog_history.summary: The seeker is dealing with disappointment after not receiving an expected overseas promotion at work, leading to feelings of stagnation and considering future career changes.

observation.content: The seeker recently found out they were not getting the overseas promotion they were expecting.
The seeker feels that their career growth isn't going as planned, which is adding to their stress.

The seeker plans to start job hunting soon but wants to be sure it's the right move before rushing into it.

dialogue.content: Hi Jane, it's good to see you here. How have you been feeling lately?

That sounds like a wise decision. Sometimes stepping back can really help clear the mind. What prompted the break?
I recently found out I wasn't getting the overseas promotion. It was a huge surprise, and honestly, I'm really struggling with it.
I'm so sorry to hear that, especially since you were expecting it. That must be incredibly frustrating and disappointing.
Yeah, it's just a mix of feeling both relieved and extremely disappointed. I guess I had my hopes up about the new opportunity.
It's completely normal to have mixed emotions, especially with something as significant as a career move. It's okay to feel both sides of it.
Thank you for saying that. It feels like my career growth isn't going as planned, and that's adding to my stress.
That's understandable, Jane. It can be very challenging to feel stagnated, especially when you've put in so much effort. How are you coping with the stress?
I guess I'm just trying to take things one day at a time. I started a journal a while back to track my thoughts and emotions, and that's been somewhat helpful.
Journaling is a fantastic way to process emotions. Have you found it easier to express your feelings on paper?
Yes, in some ways it helps, but I still feel stuck. It's like writing doesn't change the actual situation I'm in.
That's true, writing doesn't change the reality, but it can alter how you choose to navigate through it. Have you considered looking for new opportunities elsewhere?
I've thought about switching jobs due to stress before, but now I feel it's more pressing after what happened with the promotion.
It's important to prioritize your wellbeing, Jane. Taking time to consider your options and what would make you happy in your work is vital. Do you have any specific plans?
Not yet, but I might start job hunting soon. I just don't want to rush into anything. I want to be sure it's the right move for me.
That sounds sensible. Taking deliberate steps can ensure you don't end up in a similar situation. Can I help you with anything specific as you navigate this?
I think just having someone to talk to about it helps. You being here and listening makes a difference. It makes me feel less overwhelmed.
I'm really glad to hear that, Jane. You deserve to be in a place where you feel appreciated and valued. I believe you'll find that, even if it takes some time.
Thank you. I think I needed to hear that. I'll take things slow and see where it goes. Maybe this break will give me some clarity.
I hope it does, and remember, I'm always here if you need to talk or if you need any support with your future plans.
I really appreciate that. It's good to know I'm not alone in this. Thank you for being such a great friend.

dialog_history.summary: The seeker is considering moving to a new city to start fresh due to feeling stuck from work stress and family ties, but is anxious about the decision's implications.

Seeker feels stuck due to work stress, unfulfilled promotions, and certain interactions.

dialogue.content: Hey Jane, what's been on your mind lately?

Big changes? That sounds intriguing. Do you want to share more about what's driving these thoughts?
Yeah, I’m considering moving to another city. I feel stuck here, like everything is a constant reminder of what I’ve been through.
It sounds like you're looking for a fresh start. What about your current situation is making you feel stuck?
There’s just been so much—work stress, unfulfilled promotions, and interactions with people that make me feel like I’m not moving forward.
It sounds like you've been through a lot recently. Do you feel like a new city could be an opportunity to redefine things for yourself?
Exactly, a chance to leave behind some burdens and rethink what I want. But it's scary too, leaving my comfort zone, especially considering family.
Change can be daunting, especially when family is involved. How's your relationship with Eliza these days? I know that’s been important to you.
Much better after we talked things out. She's been supportive since then, but the thought of not being around for her wedding feels hard.
That sounds tough, balancing your needs with family ties. Have you talked to her about how you're feeling or this idea?
Not yet, I’m worried about how she'd react. But I know I need to eventually. I just want to make sure I’m making the right choice.
It’s understandable to want to be sure before bringing it up. What else besides family holds you back from making a move?
The fear of it all, mainly—failure, starting over, and not having a clear plan. I’ve always been one to plan everything, and this feels spontaneous.

Thanks, it's good to hear that. Sometimes, I just doubt whether I can really start fresh or if I'd be running away from my problems.
That's a valid concern. Starting anew doesn't mean your problems vanish, but it might offer a new perspective on them. Have you thought about what you want to accomplish with this move?
I want to find who I am outside of my stressors—maybe explore new career opportunities, meet new people, and just build a life that feels fulfilling.
That sounds like a beautiful goal, Jane. Focusing on your personal growth and happiness is so important. Is there a city you have in mind?
I’m thinking about San Francisco. It could be a whole new start in a place I've always admired.
San Francisco could offer a fresh start and exciting opportunities! Remember, it’s okay to take time with this decision, and talking it over with Eliza might even provide some clarity.
You’re right. I'll take my time and figure things out. Talking with Eliza might also help me see things more clearly.
Absolutely, and remember, whatever you decide, you’re not alone. I’m here to support you through it all.
Thanks so much for that. It means a lot to know someone understands what I'm going through.
Of course, Jane. Take care of yourself and reach out whenever you need to talk or reflect more on your options.

dialog_history.summary: Seeker is experiencing longing and loneliness after feeling happy for her sister at her wedding, realizing she hasn't moved on from past relationships.

observation.content: The seeker describes feeling a whirlwind of emotions since the wedding.
The seeker feels happiness and pride for her sister but also experiences longing and loneliness.
The seeker realized she hasn't fully moved on from past relationships.
The seeker is considering reaching out to a professional for support.
The seeker feels pressured to have things figured out, especially regarding her uncertain work situation.

I can imagine! Weddings can bring up so many memories and emotions. What kind of feelings are you experiencing?
Mostly happiness and pride for Eliza, but also a sense of longing and loneliness. Seeing her so happy just made me reflect on my own situation.
It's natural to reflect on your own life during such big events. It's okay to feel both joy for her and to assess your own path.
Exactly. It's hard not to compare, and I ended up thinking about my past relationships and what went wrong.
Reflecting on the past can be tough, especially when you're searching for answers. Have these thoughts led you to any new realizations or goals?
I realized I haven't fully moved on from my past relationships, and it's affecting how I view my future.

dialogue.content: Hey, are you available to chat for a bit?
Of course, Jane. What's on your mind?

I guess it's just hard to know what the right step is. I can't stop thinking about the possible repercussions if I ignore this situation at work.
Perhaps discussing this with someone you trust at work, or seeking external advice, might give you more clarity.
That might be a good idea. I just hope it doesn't backfire.
Taking measured steps could minimize potential risks. Just remember, it's okay to prioritize your principles.
Thanks for being here and listening. It helps to talk it out.
I'm always here for you, Jane. You're not alone in this.

dialog_history.summary: Jessica is struggling with a lack of motivation and difficulties in completing daily tasks, affecting her personal and professional life.

dialogue.content: Hi, how are you today?
Hi there, I'm struggling to be honest.
What are you struggling with?
I've been finding it really hard to motivate myself to do anything for the last year or so, but it's been getting worse recently. Everything feels like hard work.
To be honest, I feel the same way sometimes, too.  It is nice to have someone to talk to about this.  Have you talked to anyone else about this yet?
I haven't really, I feel like other people have their own issues and I don't want to burden them. It's good that others feel the same. Do you have any advice on what makes you feel better?
Yes.  I agree.  For me personally, I noticed if I think back of a time before I lost my motivation, sometimes it helps me to reenergize a bit.
What have motivated you in the past?

Hmm, I'm finding it hard to remember a time I didn't feel like this! I feel like this has been going on forever! I used to enjoy walking, and generally getting things done around the house. I am also self employed and loved putting time into my business but I've been finding that hard recently.
I've been watching a lot of Netflix and youtube and not doing much else.
I have been spending a lot of time home by myself as well.
How do you cope with it? How do you not get bored and restless?
I noticed if I try to adhere to a schedule, even a very simple one, such as getting up at a certain time, making breakfast, and showering.  My days tend to go better.
I've been finding I have a lot of time alone with my thoughts recently.

That's a good idea, I could try that. At the moment I get up at around 11am but U have been trying to get up earlier but I just can't make myself do it. I've also been sleeping during the day which is maybe not good.
Have you tried reading?  I find reading motivates me sometimes, too.  Sometimes too much thinking alone leaves me digging a hole for myself.
I used to get a lot of pleasure from reading and would always have a book on the go. Now reading feels like a chore, as if I am making myself do it.
I sometimes force myself to exercise when I get sleepy when I shouldn't be tired during the day.
That's a good idea I could definitely try that.
I suppose that is a little weather dependant though.
Maybe try YouTubing?  There are a lot of interesting channels that talks about science, technology, personal health, ... etc.  That can be beneficial to you and worthwhile.
I do watch a lot of youtube, but it's mainly true crime I am into. I always forget there is other content on there other than what is in my subscription box.
Certainly.  I have a pullup bar and some weights at home.  Even without those, sometimes I just do some bodyweight exercises, such as pushups, squats, ... etc.
Home workouts would be good. Do you use an app, or just make up the moves yourself?

dialogue.content: Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Jessica. How are you doing?
Honestly, not great. My health has taken a turn for the worse, and I've had to actually take a step back from work.
I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds like you're going through a tough time. How are you managing with everything?
It's been overwhelming. I knew my health wasn't the best, but I didn't expect it to get to this point where I had to pause everything.
Taking a break can be difficult, especially when you're used to being on the go. Have you been able to rest and take care of yourself?
I'm trying, but my mind keeps drifting back to work and what I'm missing. I'm afraid of what might happen in my absence.
It's natural to feel worried, but your health should come first. Have you thought about delegating some tasks to ease your mind?

Yes, I've spoken to a few trusted colleagues to keep things running. But I'm still worried something critical might slip by. I keep thinking about the time I found that discrepancy in the business accounts.
I can imagine how stressful that must have been for you. Remember, you've put systems in place and have a team to support you. They're capable.
That's true. I just feel so disconnected from everything now, and it's hard to rely on others when I'm used to doing it all myself.
Letting go of control can be hard, but sometimes stepping back gives others a chance to step up. It's a team effort now.
You're right. Maybe this is an opportunity to see how well my team can handle things. It's just so hard to shake off the anxiety.
That's understandable. What helps you manage these anxious feelings?

Meditation can take time and practice to truly help. It might also be worth talking to a professional counselor who can offer more tools and support.
I've considered that, especially since the sleep issues are getting worse again. I think I might need more structured support.
That's a really wise decision, recognizing when more help is needed. You deserve the support to get through this difficult time.
Thanks. It's relieving to have someone to talk to about this. I just hope things start looking up soon.
They will, Jessica. Take one day at a time, and give yourself the grace to heal. I'm here whenever you need to talk.
I really appreciate that. It helps to not feel so alone in all of this.
You're not alone. We're all here cheering you on and ready to support you through these challenges.
Thank you for being so supportive and patient. It means a lot.
Anytime, Jessica. Take care of yourself and reach out whenever you need to talk.
I will. Thank you again.

dialog_history.summary: Seeker is frustrated with a friend who dominates phone conversations and seeks advice on how to maintain the friendship without feeling overwhelmed.

dialogue.content: Yo
Hi, how are you doing?
I am decent. I am here because my friend talks way too much on the phone, and it frustrates me.
They never want to hang up, and the talk can literally go on for hours.
It sounds like it would be quite frustrating for your friend to talk way too much on the phone.
No, he loves it! I'm the one who hates it.
My goodness! How do they respond when you ask to end the conversation?
I tell him, but he just doesn't get it. Or, he says he understands, but then just goes back to talking!
Or, he may finally end the talk, but the next time we talk, he will just do it all over again!
I wonder what it would be like for him if you hung up the phone even after he said he still wanted to talk.
Wow--that does sound annoying that he will repeat the same pattern the next time.
He will literally talk up to 10 minutes without letting you have a word in. As far as that advice, I have hung up, but he gets extremely offended easily.
That sounds really difficult if he gets offended so easily. I find it hard to talk to some of those kinds of friends.
I'm at my wits end. I tell him all the time. "You talk too much. You gotta stop talking at me. You gotta give the other person a turn. You gotta respect other's time."
What do you get out of the friendship with this other person?
Well, I've been friends with him for a long time. He's funny and can have interesting perspectives on things. Also, we have done a lot together in the past.
That sounds like a lot that the two of you have been through. Were there other times that your friends was more equally responsive or attuned to you in conversations?
Oh, yes, I have other friends in conversations who can take turns and understand the concept of time just fine.
I just don't know what to do about this guy in particular. I still want to be his friend, but he just doesn't change.
I wonder if there is anything nice you could do for yourself when you are talking to him that would make it easier to talk to him.
Do you think I should just have a timer that goes off at 1 minute and let it beep in his face if he goes on for too long to train him like a monkey?
I can see that you are feeling upset and angry when he talks so much and that is totally understandable.
I just need a method. Talking to him is just not working.
He is hard to condition.
Would it hurt his feelings to use a timer like that? It may for some other people.
Yea, but I might be able to slip some humour in there to take the edge off because it is so silly.
Humor is really helpful for a lot of people.
Any other ideas?
Sometimes, people draw or do something else distracting with their hands when talking to someone who dominates the conversation.
So your option is to start just doing something else when he is talking? He might get the message in a subtle way?
Sometimes that is a less offensive way to retrain someone who is being obnoxious or dominant and yet who is easily offended. And, it can help preserve your sense of being grounded.
The strategy works well for me with some of my family members who seem like they will never change. But, with distraction, I enjoy them all the more.
This is true, and it isn't bade advice. Haha! That is funny. Yes, maybe I should find something to carry around with me that I can enjoy.
I don't really like to draw...
Is there anything else that you like to do that would be distracting while also letting you somewhat participate in the conversation?
Yes, perhaps I should just use the internet when he starts talking too much.
I have a phone.
That sounds really helpful. Sometimes people also play phone games or with a fidget spinner. I like your idea of looking on the internet.

This solves the problem in person, but it doesn't solve the talks over the phone, but it has been 15 minutes now and this has been helpful enough. Thank you for your solutions. You have been very supportive and kind to me
I don't want to take up any more of your time. It has been a good conversation.
You are very welcome. I wish you all the best!
Goodbye. You as well.
Bye!

Heartbreak
